notes: Two documents: the integrity-policy catalog page (stance restrict, both agreed) and the Faculty Center sample-syllabus-statements page (delegates, both agreed). Matched units are A-driven pairings; where one coder merged two sentences into one unit, the A units were each paired with that B unit. Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance, the largest, mostly require/encourage/permit vs neutral on disclosure conditions, sanction sentences and rationale (resolved: neutral when the sentence takes no position on AI use, permit when it conditions allowed use); (2) modality must vs should for polite or advisory phrasing such as 'it is important', 'please write a note', 'assume the output is incorrect' (resolved by the source wording: should); (3) phase general vs during-work for warnings about tool reliability (general); (4) policy_type for research assistance and finding sources (P12/P26 vs fit-note stretches; resolved UNCOVERED, a candidate type), translation (P18 to P91), tutorials (P44 to P70), and cited like any other reference (P24 vs P45; P45); (5) B merged some adjacent rules (ban plus plagiarism consequence, citation plus rationale, acknowledgement plus penalty) that A split; kept split since each is a distinct rule. Only-A units kept: 7 real policy statements (e.g. transparency expectation, reflection encouragement, 'let me know if you have questions'); one dropped (career-value sentence, not AI-specific). Only-B: 2 kept (writing-development rationale, office-hours help); 8 dropped in the integrity document as generic sanction tiers, plagiarism workshop, appeal right and the non-AI duty and principle sentences. Fit and uncovered notes from both coders were retained.
